profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI (also known as Ai2) is a nonprofit AI research laboratory founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. The organization describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The site notes partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the NSF on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud in support of open AI model development and scientific research platforms.

Ai2 applies its research to areas including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. The institute is led by Ali Farhadi and emphasizes deep collaboration with external organizations as central to its approach to building advanced, open AI.

The two AI products tracked for Ai2 are OLMo, an open-source large language model developed with fully open training data and a focus on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an AI-powered academic search tool offering paper summaries and citation graphs oriented toward nonprofit research use. No litigation, MCP servers, SEC filings, or patent records are held for the organization.
